compiled_state.description:
## Context
Split from 36d1, which forces a fetch for the review-start snapshot and the pre-lock collect in sign_manifest. The claim-time currency check (`rebar review-plan <id> --status`, and the claim gate that reads the same attestation currency) still goes through `ensure_fresh` on the 60 s throttle, so within that window it can judge an attestation current against a clone that is behind origin.

## Not yet established
No reproduction yet. Needs a two-repo store like tests/unit/test_read_freshness_parity.py: origin edits the description after the attestation, the throttle marker is fresh, and claim/--status is evaluated on the lagging clone. Whether a claim is actually granted on stale material, or only the read-only status is wrong, is unchecked.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A test shows whether claim or --status accepts an attestation whose plan material was changed on origin inside the throttle window.
- [ ] If it does, the claim-time check forces one fetch before judging currency, and the default throttle for other reads is unchanged.
compiled_state.title: Claim-time plan-review currency check can read a tickets clone up to 60 s behind origin
